definition: An organized division of the church, a place appointed for the gathering of the Saints, serving as a support and strength to Zion like a tent stake.
A standing body of priesthood holders or appointed officers organized under a president and counselors to act together, as the quorum of the Twelve or the quorum of the Nauvoo House.
To wet thoroughly or steep in a liquid, as a sword bathed in heaven or the moon bathed in blood.
The kidneys or loins, regarded as the seat of the deepest thoughts, feelings and conscience.
A binding agreement between God and his people, ratified by sacrifice or blood, as in the new testament in my blood.
To register a person in a official census or enrollment of the population, which was also the basis for taxation.
To ask earnestly or plead with someone, so that easy to be entreated means open to appeals and persuasion.
One who melts and casts metal into images or vessels; a metalworker.
One who sets up or originates something, such as a church, a city or a practice.
